--- title: "Covariance, Correlation, and Scatterplots" subtitle: "PSYC 6019-A01 / PSYC 6022-A01
2026-11-13 | Lab 12" author: "Jess Helmer" footer: "[jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026](https://jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026/)" format: revealjs: code-link: true slide-number: true code-line-numbers: false theme: ../../gt-theme.scss width: 1200 execute: echo: true dpi: 600 freeze: auto knitr: opts_chunk: dev: svg --- ## Outline - Correlation - Scatterplots - Scatterplot matrices - Simple regression ::: {.cell} ::: # Correlation ## Correlation So far, we've been talking about continuous outcomes as predicted by different **categorical** variables. But the world is not limited to categorical predictors! Today, we are going to talk about estimating associations between two continuous variables by examining their **correlation**. ## Correlation Correlation is a measure of the **linear association** between two continuous variables. Is a standardized version of **covariance**. ## Covariance Covariance is an unstandardized index of the linear relationship between two continuous variables. $$ s_{xy} = \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^N (x_i - \bar{x}) (y_i - \bar{y}) }{N - 1} $$ ::: subpoint ○ $x_i$: an observation of $x$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $\bar{x}$: sample mean of $x$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $y_i$: an observation of $y$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $\bar{y}$: sample mean of $y$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $N$: sample size ::: *The deviations of each $x_i$ from its mean and the deviations of each $y_i$ from its mean, multiplied together, summed up, and divided by the sample size minus one.* ## Covariance Visually Examples of positive, zero, and negative covariance: ::: {.cell layout-ncol="3" layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-2.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-3.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ## Correlation It's tricky to numerically interpret a covariance, because it is in a combination of x and y's units. Correlation standardizes covariance down to a single scale. $$ r_{xy} = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_{x} s_{y}} $$ ::: subpoint ○ $s_{xy}$: covariance between $x$ and $y$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $s_x$: sample standard deviation of $x$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $s_y$: sample standard deviation of $y$ ::: We standardize covariance into correlation just by dividing by the two variables' standard deviations! ## Correlation It's tricky to numerically interpret a covariance, because it is in a combination of x and y's units. Correlation standardizes covariance down to a single scale. $$ r_{xy} = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_{x} s_{y}} = \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^N (x_i - \bar{x}) (y_i - \bar{y}) }{\sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^N (x_i - \bar{x})^2} \sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^N (y_i - \bar{y})^2}}$$ Bounded from $[-1, \ 1]$ ::: subpoint ○ $r_{xy} = -1$: strong negative correlation (when $x$ increases, $y$ tends to decrease) ::: ::: subpoint ○ $r_{xy} = 0$: no correlation ($x$ increasing doesn't provide information about $y$) ::: ::: subpoint ○ $r_{xy} = 1$: strong positive correlation (when $x$ increases, $y$ tends to increase) ::: ## Covariance in R `cov(x, y = NULL, use = "everything", method = "pearson")` ::: subpoint ○ `x` = numeric vector or dataframe ::: ::: subpoint ○ `y` = if `x` is a numeric vector, can specify `y` as a numeric vector ::: ::: subpoint ○ `use` = how to handle missing (`NA`) values ::: ::: subpoint ○ `method` = which type of coefficient to compute ::: ## Covariance in R Need to `select()` down just to variables of interest. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cov() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm NA NA body_mass_g NA NA ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cov(use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 197.7318 9824.416 body_mass_g 9824.4161 643131.077 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Correlation in R `cor(x, y = NULL, use = "everything", method = "pearson")` ::: subpoint ○ `x` = numeric vector or dataframe ::: ::: subpoint ○ `y` = if `x` is a numeric vector, can specify `y` as a numeric vector ::: ::: subpoint ○ `use` = how to handle missing (`NA`) values ::: ::: subpoint ○ `method` = which type of coefficient to compute ::: ## Correlation in R :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1 NA body_mass_g NA 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Handling `NA`s `cov()` and `cor()` have different options for what to do if missing values (`NA`s) are present ::: subpoint ○ `"everything"` = use all values: if one is `NA`, result will be `NA` ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"all.obs"` = use all values: if one is `NA` throw an error ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"complete.obs"` = delete rows with any `NA` values at all: if no rows remaining, throw an error ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"na.or.complete"` = delete rows with any `NA` values at all: if no rows remaining, result will be `NA` ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"pairwise.complete.obs"` = for each pair of variables, delete rows if either of the pairs is `NA`: may result in correlations being computed on different sample sizes ::: ## Handling `NA`s :::: {.columns style="font-size:90%"} ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "everything") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1 NA body_mass_g NA 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "all.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `cor()`: ! missing observations in cov/cor ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: :::: {.columns style="font-size:90%"} ::: {.column width="17%"} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "na.or.complete") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="17%"} ::: :::: ## Testing Correlations ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("rstatix") penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> rstatix::cor_test() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 9 var1 var2 cor statistic df p conf.low conf.high method 1 flipper_lengt… body… 0.87 32.7 340 4.37e-107 0.843 0.895 Pears… ``` ::: ::: ## Ordinal Correlations :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_ordinal <- penguins |> mutate( across( c(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm), function(bill_column) case_when( bill_column < quantile(bill_column, .33, na.rm = T) ~ "low", between( bill_column, quantile(bill_column, 1/3, na.rm = T), quantile(bill_column, 2/3, na.rm = T) ) ~ "med", bill_column > quantile(bill_column, .66, na.rm = T) ~ "high" ) |> factor(levels = c("low", "med", "high"), ordered = TRUE), .names = "{.col}_ordinal" ) ) |> select(ends_with("_ordinal")) head(penguins_ordinal) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 2 bill_length_mm_ordinal bill_depth_mm_ordinal 1 low high 2 low med 3 low med 4 5 low high 6 low high ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_ordinal |> count(bill_length_mm_ordinal, bill_depth_mm_ordinal) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 10 × 3 bill_length_mm_ordinal bill_depth_mm_ordinal n 1 low low 5 2 low med 59 3 low high 49 4 med low 53 5 med med 30 6 med high 32 7 high low 55 8 high med 28 9 high high 31 10 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Ordinal Correlations :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_ordinal |> mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |> cor(use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` bill_length_mm_ordinal bill_depth_mm_ordinal bill_length_mm_ordinal 1.0000000 -0.3009783 bill_depth_mm_ordinal -0.3009783 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_ordinal |> mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |> cor(use = "complete.obs", method = "kendall") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` bill_length_mm_ordinal bill_depth_mm_ordinal bill_length_mm_ordinal 1.0000000 -0.2676226 bill_depth_mm_ordinal -0.2676226 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-25-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + labs(y = "Body Mass", x = "Flipper Length") + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} If there are lots of datapoints, may want to take down the `alpha` for clearer results. E.g., with the `tidyverse` `diamonds` dataset. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-27-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = carat, y = price)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.025, shape = 16, size = 2) + labs(y = "Price", x = "Carat") + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency()) + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-29-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} r <- cor(penguins$flipper_length_mm, penguins$body_mass_g, use = "complete.obs") penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + annotate(geom = "text", label = round(r, 2), x = mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T), y = max(penguins$body_mass_g, na.rm = T)) + labs(y = "Body Mass", x = "Flipper Length") + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-31-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} r <- cor(penguins$flipper_length_mm, penguins$body_mass_g, use = "complete.obs") r_label <- paste("italic(r) ==", round(r, 2)) penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + annotate(geom = "text", label = r_label, x = mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T), y = max(penguins$body_mass_g, na.rm = T), parse = T) + labs(y = "Body Mass", x = "Flipper Length") + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Adding a **regression line**. Defines the relationship between the variables as $y = mx + b$ ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $b$: intercept, $y$ when $x = 0$ ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $m$: slope, change in $y$ with unit increase in $x$ ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-33-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} r <- cor(penguins$flipper_length_mm, penguins$body_mass_g, use = "complete.obs") r_label <- paste("italic(r) ==", round(r, 2)) penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "seagreen", fill = "seagreen") + annotate(geom = "text", label = r_label, x = mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T), y = max(penguins$body_mass_g, na.rm = T), parse = T) + labs(y = "Body Mass", x = "Flipper Length") + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplot Matrices :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-35-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("GGally") penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> GGally::ggpairs() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplot Matrices :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-37-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm) |> GGally::ggpairs() + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplot Matrices :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Adding a LOESS line... ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-39-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm) |> GGally::ggpairs() + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplot Matrices :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-41-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} custom_trendline <- function(data, mapping, ...) { ggplot(data = data, mapping = mapping) + geom_point(...) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") } penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm) |> GGally::ggpairs(lower = list(continuous = custom_trendline)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: # Simple Regression ## Simple Regression When we added trendlines (`method = "lm"`) onto our scatterplots, we were performing a **regression**. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="75%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-43-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(1) tibble( x = rnorm(100, 5, 1.5), y = 3 + 2 * x + rnorm(100, 0, 3) ) |> ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2), limits = c(0, 10)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5), limits = c(0, 25)) + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="75%"} We are representing the relationship between the variables as $y = mx + b$. ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $b$: intercept, $y$ when $x = 0$ ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $m$: slope, change in $y$ with unit increase in $x$ ::: ::: :::: ## Simple Regression When we added trendlines (`method = "lm"`) onto our scatterplots, we were performing a **regression**. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="75%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-45-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(1) d <- tibble( x = rnorm(100, 5, 1.5), y = 3 + 2 * x + rnorm(100, 0, 3) ) fit <- lm(y ~ x, data = d) b0 <- coef(fit)[[1]] b1 <- coef(fit)[[2]] grey <- "grey25" arr <- arrow(length = unit(0.09, "inches"), type = "closed") # One-unit run (x = 8 to 9) and the corresponding rise x0 <- 7 x1 <- 8 y0 <- b0 + b1 * x0 y1 <- b0 + b1 * x1 ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.6, shape = 16, size = 1.8, color = "steelblue") + geom_abline(intercept = b0, slope = b1, color = "pink3", linewidth = 0.8) + # Intercept: point where the line crosses x = 0, with a curved arrow and label annotate("point", x = 0, y = b0, color = "black", size = 3) + annotate("curve", x = 1.6, xend = 0.15, y = b0 + 6, yend = b0 + 0.5, curvature = 0.35, arrow = arr, color = grey, linewidth = 0.5) + annotate("text", x = 1.7, y = b0 + 6.8, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5, parse = TRUE, label = sprintf("beta[0] == %.2f", b0)) + # Slope: one-unit run, then the rise over that run annotate("segment", x = x0, xend = x1, y = y0, yend = y0, linetype = "dashed", color = grey, linewidth = 0.4) + geom_errorbar(data = tibble(x = x1 + 0.12, ymin = y0, ymax = y1), aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), width = 0.15, color = grey, linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) + annotate("text", x = x1 + 0.3, y = (y0 + y1) / 2, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5, parse = TRUE, label = sprintf("beta[1] == %.2f", b1)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2), limits = c(0, 10)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5), limits = c(0, 25)) + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = TRUE), y = guide_axis(cap = TRUE)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="75%"} We are representing the relationship between the variables as $y = mx + b$. ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $b$: intercept, $y$ when $x = 0$ ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $m$: slope, change in $y$ with unit increase in $x$ ::: In modeling, you more often see this as $y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ ::: subpoint-narrow ○ General linear model ::: ::: :::: ## Regression Example Let's regress penguin bill length ($x$) on penguin bill depth ($y$). $$\text{bill depth}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{bill length}_i + \epsilon_i$$ :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bill_model <- lm(bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins) summary(bill_model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -4.1381 -1.4263 0.0164 1.3841 4.5255 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 20.88547 0.84388 24.749 < 2e-16 *** bill_length_mm -0.08502 0.01907 -4.459 1.12e-05 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 1.922 on 340 degrees of freedom (2 observations deleted due to missingness) Multiple R-squared: 0.05525, Adjusted R-squared: 0.05247 F-statistic: 19.88 on 1 and 340 DF, p-value: 1.12e-05 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} $R^2 = \frac{\mathrm{SS}_\mathrm{regression}}{\mathrm{SS}_y} = \frac{\sum(\hat{y}_i - \bar{y})}{\sum(\hat{y}_i- \bar{y})}$ ::: subpoint-narrow ○ Proportion of variance in $y$ explained by the model (predicted values $\hat{y}$) ::: ::: :::: ## `lm()` Objects :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bill_model_tidy <- broom::tidy(bill_model) bill_model_tidy ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) 20.9 0.844 24.7 4.72e-78 2 bill_length_mm -0.0850 0.0191 -4.46 1.12e- 5 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bill_model |> gtsummary::tbl_regression(intercept = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Now, $\text{bill length} = 0$ means the *average* bill length across penguins. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_cleaned <- penguins |> mutate(across(c(starts_with("bill_")), scale, .names = "{.col}_z")) penguins_cleaned |> select(starts_with("bill_")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 344 × 4 bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm bill_length_mm_z[,1] bill_depth_mm_z[,1] 1 39.1 18.7 -0.883 0.784 2 39.5 17.4 -0.810 0.126 3 40.3 18 -0.663 0.430 4 NA NA NA NA 5 36.7 19.3 -1.32 1.09 6 39.3 20.6 -0.847 1.75 7 38.9 17.8 -0.920 0.329 8 39.2 19.6 -0.865 1.24 9 34.1 18.1 -1.80 0.480 10 42 20.2 -0.352 1.54 # ℹ 334 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Standardized Regression :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="66%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} options(scipen = 999) bill_model_z <- lm(bill_depth_mm_z ~ bill_length_mm_z, data = penguins_cleaned) broom::tidy(bill_model_z) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), function(x) round(x, 3))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) 0 0.053 0 1 2 bill_length_mm_z -0.235 0.053 -4.46 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cor( penguins_cleaned$bill_length_mm, penguins_cleaned$bill_depth_mm, use = "complete.obs" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] -0.2350529 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: [Simple regression slope coefficient is just the correlation!]{.fragment fragment-index=1} ![](https://i.pinimg.com/736x/a2/42/d8/a242d89f5bfca11a69c2f0a4fa3fb995.jpg){.absolute bottom = 0, right = 0 .fragment fragment-index=1} ## Next Week More regression! :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Visualizing regression predictions Assumption checking Regression diagnostics Confounders ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](https://64.media.tumblr.com/6509cc0d5bcf66cb1bc671048246d312/bfe1c51976b5c5ed-2a/s540x810/c7f448c88271b7cc79d3e005d1e50c5e83a56312.gifv) ::: :::: ## Lab 12 Activity

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
